s.d: the result of having corrected a wrong or bad situation
s.c: In some languages ‘reforms’ may be rendered as ‘changes from bad to good’ or ‘making things what they should be’ or ‘causing new good customs.’

s.d: to express an unusually high degree of confidence in someone or something being exceptionally noteworthy{N:001}
s.c: Whether in any particular context the boasting is legitimate or not depends upon what is boasted about. In a number of languages, however, quite different terms are employed, depending upon the differing degrees of justification for such boasting.

s.d: to express an unusually high degree of confidence in someone or something being exceptionally noteworthy{N:001}
s.c: Whether in any particular context the boasting is legitimate or not depends upon what is boasted about. In a number of languages, however, quite different terms are employed, depending upon the differing degrees of justification for such boasting.

s.g: to be sound asleep; to be completely asleep

s.d: to kiss, either as an expression of greeting or as a sign of special affection and appreciation{N:001}
s.c: Since in so many societies kissing is not a form of greeting, it may be necessary to add some kind of classifier to contexts such as ⟦Matthew 26:48|Matthew 26:48⟧ and ⟦Matthew 26:49|Matthew 26:49⟧ in order to indicate clearly the intention involved; otherwise, the use of a term meaning merely ‘to kiss’ might suggest a kind of erotic display. The clause in ⟦Matthew 26:49|Matthew 26:49⟧ may be translated as ‘the man I greet by kissing is the one you want.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Despise, Scorn, Contempt

s.g: to despise; to scorn; to look down on
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘to despise’ is ‘to think that something has no value’ or ‘to reckon something as being worthless.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Despise, Scorn, Contempt
s.d: (derivative of {L:καταφρονέω<SDBG:καταφρονέω:000000>} ‘to despise,’ {D:88.192}) one who customarily feels contempt for something or someone
s.c: The equivalent of ‘scoffer’ may be ‘one who always talks against’ or ‘one who thinks nothing is ever any good.’

s.dp: Activities Involving Liquids or Masses › Movement of Liquids or Masses
s.d: to cause to pour down on

s.c: In ⟦Philippians 2:10|Philippians 2:10⟧ καταχθονίων is probably a reference to the dead, generally regarded as inhabiting a dark region under the ground.

s.c: In some languages it may be necessary to render this expression in ⟦Luke 16:24|Luke 16:24⟧ as ‘to cause my tongue to feel cool.’

s.c: In place of the traditional rendering ‘how full of idols their city was,’ one may have ‘how many idols there were in their city’ or ‘how many idols the people worshiped there in their city.’

s.g: in the sight of; in the opinion of; in the judgment of

s.g: to cause to be; to make to be; to make; to result in; to bring upon; to bring about

s.d: to cause to be thoroughly prepared
to move down, irrespective of the gradient
s.g: to move down; to come down; to go down; to descend
s.c: In a number of languages there is a series of terms for going down or descending, depending upon the gradient and the rapidity with which someone or something descends. There may also be distinct terms depending upon the extent of the descent. Rain coming down would be regarded as an extensive descent, while getting out of a boat to walk on the water would be a very limited descent.|Movement downward may, of course, involve more than physical objects, for example, οὐκ ἔστιν αὕτη ἡ σοφία ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη ‘this is not the wisdom that comes down from above’ ⟦James 3:15|James 3:15⟧. Since in ⟦James 3:15|James 3:15⟧ ἄνωθεν is a substitute for God, it may be necessary to restructure this statement as ‘this wisdom does not come from God’ or ‘God is not the source of this wisdom.’

s.d: (technical, nautical term) to go by ship toward the shore
s.g: to arrive at land; to put in at

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Eat, Drink
s.d: to devour something completely
s.c: In some languages a distinction is made in terms referring to eating by birds in contrast with eating by animals or people.

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:κατεσθίω<SDBG:κατεσθίω:000000>}[a] ‘to eat up,’ {D:23.11}) to destroy completely (in a sense more emphatic than {L:ἐσθίω<SDBG:ἐσθίω:000001>}[b], {D:20.44})
s.g: to destroy utterly; to consume completely

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:κατεσθίω<SDBG:κατεσθίω:000000>}[a] ‘to eat up, to consume,’ {D:23.11}) to take over by dishonest means the property of someone else
(a figurative extension of meaning of {L:κατεσθίω<SDBG:κατεσθίω:000000>}[a] ‘to eat up, to consume,’ {D:23.11}) to spend or use up excessively and uselessly

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Exploit
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:κατεσθίω<SDBG:κατεσθίω:000000>}[a] ‘to eat up,’ {D:23.11}) to take total advantage of someone
s.g: to exploit completely; to take complete advantage of

s.d: to so influence others as to cause them to follow a recommended course of action
s.g: to guide; to direct; to lead
s.c: In some languages it is difficult to distinguish readily between expressions for ‘leading’ and those which refer to ‘ruling’ or ‘governing,’ but it is important to try to distinguish clearly between these two different sets of interpersonal relations. In some languages, the concept of ‘leading’ can be expressed by ‘showing how to’ or ‘demonstrating how one ought to.’ In other languages it is possible to speak of ‘leading’ as simply ‘going ahead of,’ but too often such an expression may designate only ‘a scout’ who goes ahead to see whether things are safe, or it may refer only to a person who insists on his prerogative as the most distinguished person in a group.

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Behavior, Conduct
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to guide the feet properly) to guide or direct behavior in an appropriate manner
s.g: to guide; to direct; to make to live

s.d: to use sudden physical force against someone as the outgrowth of a hostile attitude{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘to attack’ is simply ‘to start fighting against.’ In some languages, however, the equivalent is ‘to jump on’ or ‘to grab to do harm to.’

s.d: to prevent someone from doing something by restraining or hindering
s.g: to prevent; to hinder; to restrain; to keep from

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Believe To Be True
s.d: to continue to believe, with the implication of acting in accordance with such belief
s.g: to continue to believe and practice; to continue to follow

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Have, Possess, Property, Owner
s.d: to have or possess objects or property (in the technical sense of having control over the use of such objects){N:001}{N:002}
s.g: to have; to own; to possess; to belong to

s.d: to exercise continuous control over someone or something
s.c: There is usually no difficulty in speaking of ‘control’ if it is performed by a person as in ⟦1 Peter 2:13|1 Peter 2:13⟧. However, it may not be possible to speak of ‘death’ having control, unless the language in question can personify death. In some instances ⟦Acts 2:24|Acts 2:24⟧ (see LN 37.16) must be rendered as ‘it was impossible for him to continue to be dead,’ and in ⟦2 Corinthians 5:14|2 Corinthians 5:14⟧ ‘Christ’s love controls us’ may be rendered as ‘the fact that Christ loves us causes us to act as we do.’

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to come to occupy a particular place
s.g: to come to be in a place; to occupy

s.d: (a nautical idiom, literally: to control toward) to control the movement of a ship to a particular point
to bring serious charges or accusations against someone, with the possible connotation of a legal or court context{N:001}
(derivative of {L:κατηγορέω<SDBG:κατηγορέω:000000>} ‘to accuse,’ {D:33.427}) the content of the accusation or charge made against someone
s.c: It is possible that in ⟦1 Timothy 5:19|1 Timothy 5:19⟧ κατηγορία may denote either the event of accusing or the content of the accusation. If κατηγορία in ⟦1 Timothy 5:19|1 Timothy 5:19⟧ is understood as the event of accusing, it may be classified with the items in LN 33.427.

s.d: (derivative of {L:κατηγορέω<SDBG:κατηγορέω:000000>} ‘to accuse,’ {D:33.427}) one who brings accusation
(derivative of {L:κατηγορέω<SDBG:κατηγορέω:000000>} ‘to accuse,’ {D:33.427}) one who brings accusation
a state of mental gloominess and dejection
s.c: In a number of languages it may be extremely difficult to speak of ‘changing’ one activity into another or one state into another, and so this expression in ⟦James 4:9|James 4:9⟧ must often be rendered as ‘instead of laughing, mourn, and instead of being happy, become sad.’

s.d: to teach in a systematic or detailed manner
s.c: It is also possible to understand κατηχέω in ⟦Luke 1:4|Luke 1:4⟧ as denoting merely what has been told rather than what has been taught (see κατηχέω, LN 33.190). This distinction is an important one since it implies a quite different relationship of Theophilus to the text of the Gospel of Luke. If ⟦Luke 1:4|Luke 1:4⟧ pertains merely to Theophilus ‘being told’ something, then one might assume that Theophilus was not a Christian, in which case he may have been a government official to whom the joint publications (the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles) would have been directed as a defense of Christianity. On the other hand, if one understands κατηχέω in the sense of ‘to be taught’ or ‘to be instructed,’ then one would assume that Theophilus was a Christian who had been instructed in the faith. The relationship of Theophilus to the message would then determine in a number of contexts the difference between ‘we’ inclusive and ‘we’ exclusive.

s.d: to report in a relatively detailed manner
s.g: to report; to tell; to in form
s.c: It is also possible to understand κατηχέω in ⟦Luke 1:4|Luke 1:4⟧ as systematic teaching (see LN 33.225).

s.d: to undergo the process of oxidation of metals
s.g: to become rusty; to become tarnished; to corrode
s.c: See discussion at LN 2.60.

s.d: to be completely capable of doing or experiencing something
s.g: to be completely able; to be fully able
s.c: For another interpretation of κατισχύω in ⟦Luke 21:36|Luke 21:36⟧, see LN 79.64.

s.d: to be physically strong enough for some purpose
s.g: to be strong enough to; to be able to; to have the strength to
s.c: For another interpretation of κατισχύω in ⟦Luke 21:36|Luke 21:36⟧, see LN 74.10.

s.d: to prevail over something or some person so as to be able to defeat, with the implication that the successful participant has greater strength
s.c: In some languages it may be impossible to personify ‘death’ and thus make it an agent of ‘defeating.’ However, it is possible to retain some of the figurative meaning involved, at least in some languages, by translating ‘and my church will never die out’ or ‘and my church will never die.’

s.d: to live or dwell in a place in an established or settled manner
s.g: to live; to dwell; to reside
s.c: The quotation from ⟦Psalms 69:25|Psalms 69:25⟧ in ⟦Acts 1:20|Acts 1:20⟧ normally requires a literal rendering, but the entire passage is figurative.

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of κατοικίζω ‘to cause to dwell,’ not occurring in the NT) to cause to be in a place defined psychologically or spiritually
s.g: to put within; to cause to dwell

s.d: (derivative of {L:κατοικέω<SDBG:κατοικέω:000000>} ‘to dwell,’ {D:85.69}) a place of dwelling, whether an object or area{N:001}
(derivative of {L:κατοικέω<SDBG:κατοικέω:000000>} ‘to dwell,’ {D:85.69}) a place of dwelling, whether an object or area{N:001}
(derivative of {L:κατοικέω<SDBG:κατοικέω:000000>} ‘to dwell,’ {D:85.69}) a place of dwelling, whether an object or area{N:001}
to see indirectly or by reflection as in a mirror
s.g: to see as in a mirror; to see by reflection
s.c: The phrase ‘as in a mirror’ may be translated in some languages as ‘as though we were looking into a mirror’ or ‘as though what we saw was in a mirror.’ In some languages, however, one does not say ‘in a mirror’ but ‘through a mirror’ or ‘by means of a mirror.’ For another interpretation of κατοπτρίζομαι in ⟦2 Corinthians 3:18|2 Corinthians 3:18⟧, see LN 14.52.

s.d: to reflect light or visual patterns coming from some source
s.c: In order to speak of a reflection of light, it may be necessary to say ‘to throw back the light’ or ‘to shine back the form.’ Sometimes it is necessary to stipulate a type of object which reflects such light, for example, ‘we are a shining object that shows back the glory of the Lord.’ For another interpretation of κατοπτρίζομαι in ⟦2 Corinthians 3:18|2 Corinthians 3:18⟧, see LN 24.44.

s.d: a position immediately or directly below a point of orientation, which is often left implicit
s.c: In a number of languages it is not possible to speak of something ‘below’ without indicating precisely what is involved, but in the case of ⟦Acts 2:19|Acts 2:19⟧ it would be irrelevant to say ‘marvels on the earth below the sky.’ Therefore, one may perhaps most satisfactorily translate this expression in ⟦Acts 2:19|Acts 2:19⟧ as ‘marvels here on the earth.’

s.dp: Spacial Extensions › Extension To a Goal
s.d: extension toward a goal which is down or below
pertaining to a lesser amount or extent
pertaining to being in a position below a point of orientation
s.c: See discussion at LN 1.18.

s.d: heat sufficiently intense to cause suffering or burning
s.c: In some languages the effect of heat may be described simply as ‘heat will not scorch them’ or ‘they will not suffer because of heat’ (⟦Revelation 7:16|Revelation 7:16⟧). Such expressions, however, may be ambiguous because they might mean that the individuals involved would be able to easily withstand the heat. The meaning of the biblical passage, however, is that there would be no heat to cause them harm.

s.d: to cause to suffer because of intense heat
s.g: to harm by heat; to scorch

s.d: the process of burning
s.g: to burn; burning; to be on fire
s.c: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in the use of terms for burning. For example, the burning of a substance for light, as in the case of a lamp or candle, may be indicated by a term quite different from an expression indicating the destruction or burning up of something. Similarly, the burning of wood for cooking may require still another term. The extent or size of the fire involved may also require some distinctions in terms for burning.

s.d: the process of burning
s.g: to burn; burning; to be on fire
s.c: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in the use of terms for burning. For example, the burning of a substance for light, as in the case of a lamp or candle, may be indicated by a term quite different from an expression indicating the destruction or burning up of something. Similarly, the burning of wood for cooking may require still another term. The extent or size of the fire involved may also require some distinctions in terms for burning.

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to be seared in the conscience, or: to be seared as to one’s conscience) to be unwilling to learn from one’s conscience
s.g: to refuse to listen to one’s conscience; to be completely insensitive to

s.d: heat sufficiently intense to cause suffering or burning
s.c: In some languages the effect of heat may be described simply as ‘heat will not scorch them’ or ‘they will not suffer because of heat.’ Such expressions, however, may be ambiguous because they might mean that the individuals involved would be able to easily withstand the heat. The meaning of the biblical passage, however, is that there would be no heat to cause them harm.

s.d: to express an unusually high degree of confidence in someone or something being exceptionally noteworthy{N:001}
s.c: Whether in any particular context the boasting is legitimate or not depends upon what is boasted about. In a number of languages, however, quite different terms are employed, depending upon the differing degrees of justification for such boasting.

s.d: (derivative of {L:καυχάομαι<SDBG:καυχάομαι:000000>} ‘to boast,’ {D:33.368}) the referent of boasting, namely, that which one boasts about
s.c: For another interpretation of καύχημα in ⟦2 Corinthians 1:14|2 Corinthians 1:14⟧, see LN 25.203.

s.d: the justification for boasting
the basis for or the content of one’s feeling of legitimate pride
s.g: basis of pride; reason for being proud
s.c: For another interpretation of καύχημα in ⟦2 Corinthians 1:14|2 Corinthians 1:14⟧, see LN 33.371.

s.d: to express an unusually high degree of confidence in someone or something being exceptionally noteworthy{N:001}
s.c: Whether in any particular context the boasting is legitimate or not depends upon what is boasted about. In a number of languages, however, quite different terms are employed, depending upon the differing degrees of justification for such boasting.

s.d: (derivative of {L:καυχάομαι<SDBG:καυχάομαι:000000>} ‘to boast,’ {D:33.368}) the referent of boasting, namely, that which one boasts about
the state of being rightfully proud

s.d: a seaport of the city of Corinth

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a valley between Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives

s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Lie
s.d: to be in a lying or reclining position

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to be in a place, frequently in the sense of ‘being contained in’ or ‘resting on’
to exist, with the implication of having been established and thus having continuity and purpose
s.g: to exist; to exist for; to be set

s.dp: Artifacts › Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
s.d: small piece of cloth; used for wrapping something
s.g: band of cloth; strip of cloth
s.c: In ⟦John 11:44|John 11:44⟧ one may translate ‘the strips of cloth that had been put around the body of Lazarus.’

s.d: to cut the hair of a person or animal
(derivative of {L:κελεύω<SDBG:κελεύω:000000>} ‘to command,’ {D:33.323}) the voicing of a command
s.c: In a number of languages the expression ‘at the word of command’ may be rendered as ‘when the command is given’ or ‘when the command is shouted.’

s.d: to state with force and/or authority what others must do
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘to order’ or ‘to command’ is ‘to speak with strength’ or ‘to speak strong words’ or, in the form of direct discourse, ‘to tell others, You must …’

s.d: a state of pride which is without basis or justification
s.g: empty pride; cheap pride; vain pride

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Arrogance, Haughtiness, Pride
s.d: pertaining to being proud without basis or justification
s.c: It is often possible to render ‘to be falsely proud’ as ‘to be proud when there is no reason to be proud’ or ‘to be proud even when there is nothing to be proud of.’

s.d: pertaining to being without anything

s.dp: Understand › Lack of Capacity for Understanding
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:κενός<SDBG:κενός:000000>}[a] ‘empty,’ {D:57.42}) pertaining to a complete lack of understanding and insight
pertaining to being lacking in results
s.c: In ⟦1 Corinthians 15:14|1 Corinthians 15:14⟧, one may understand purpose rather than result, and hence one can translate ‘our message is indeed without purpose’ (see LN 89.64). For yet another interpretation of κενός in ⟦1 Corinthians 15:14|1 Corinthians 15:14⟧, see LN 72.10.

s.d: pertaining to being totally without purpose
s.c: For other interpretations of κενός in ⟦1 Corinthians 15:14|1 Corinthians 15:14⟧, see LN 72.10 and LN 89.53.

s.d: pertaining to being untrue in view of lacking truth
s.c: For other interpretations of κενός in ⟦1 Corinthians 15:14|1 Corinthians 15:14⟧, see LN 89.53 and LN 89.64.

s.d: talk which lacks significant content
s.c: ‘Foolish talk’ may often be expressed as ‘to talk the way fools talk’ or ‘to talk with a smirk on the face.’

s.d: to take away the power or significance of something
s.g: to cause to lose power; to cause to be emptied of power; to make powerless

s.dp: Status › Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
s.d: to completely remove or eliminate elements of high status or rank by eliminating all privileges or prerogatives associated with such status or rank
s.g: to empty oneself; to divest oneself of position

s.d: a sharp, pointed projection used in stinging

s.dp: Artifacts › Instruments Used in Agriculture and Husbandry
s.d: a pointed stick used in driving draft animals
s.c: In the NT κέντρον occurs only in the idiom πρὸς κέντρον λακτίζειν 'to kick against the goad;' meaning to hurt oneself by active resistance. See LN 39.19.

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:κέντρον<SDBG:κέντρον:000000>}[a] ‘sting,’ {D:8.45}) the power or ability to kill or destroy
s.g: power to kill; power to destroy
s.c: For another interpretation of κέντρον in ⟦1 Corinthians 15:55|1 Corinthians 15:55⟧, see LN 24.86.

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Pain, Suffering
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:κέντρον<SDBG:κέντρον:000000>}[a] ‘sting,’ {D:8.45}) the means or capacity to cause severe suffering
s.g: means to hurt; power to cause suffering
s.c: For another interpretation of κέντρον in ⟦1 Corinthians 15:55|1 Corinthians 15:55⟧, see LN 20.69.

s.d: a Roman officer in command of about one hundred men
s.c: In a number of languages, centurion can very readily be rendered by a phrase such as ‘a commander of a hundred soldiers,’ but in many instances the closest natural equivalent is simply ‘captain.’

s.d: pertaining to being totally without purpose
a part of a letter of the alphabet
s.g: stroke; short mark; short line of a letter; part of a letter
s.c: The reference of ἰῶτα (LN 33.36) and κεραία is to the small details of the Law, and therefore it may be appropriate in many languages to translate ⟦Matthew 5:18|Matthew 5:18⟧ as ‘not one of the smallest parts of the Law will be done away with’ or ‘… will become null and void.’

s.d: (derivative of {L:κεράμιον<SDBG:κεράμιον:000000>} ‘earthenware vessel,’ {D:6.128}) one who makes earthenware vessels

s.dp: Natural Substances › Earth, Mud, Sand, Rock
s.d: (derivative of {L:κέραμος<SDBG:κέραμος:000000>} ‘potter’s clay,’ not occurring in the NT) pertaining to being made of potter’s clay
s.c: In some languages it may seem unduly repetitious to speak of ‘clay pots’ in ⟦Revelation 2:27|Revelation 2:27⟧ since a term for pot may refer only to objects made of clay. In biblical times, however, some σκεύη were of metal and others were of stone and wood. It may be possible to translate this expression in ⟦Revelation 2:27|Revelation 2:27⟧ as ‘they shall be broken like pots’ or ‘… like dishes.’

s.d: an earthenware container for storing or carrying liquids
a thin slab or bent piece of baked clay; used to cover a roof
to mix substances, normally liquids
s.c: Note that in the process of mixing, the various substances become a single mass, and the constituent parts are indistinguishable. For another interpretation of κεράννυμι in ⟦Revelation 14:10|Revelation 14:10⟧, see LN 47.3.

s.dp: Activities Involving Liquids or Masses › Movement of Liquids or Masses
s.d: to pour something out
s.c: Since κεράννυμι normally means ‘to mix,’ it is possible to interpret the participial form κεκερασμένου in ⟦Revelation 14:10|Revelation 14:10⟧ as meaning ‘to be mixed’ (see LN 63.9), but this would seem to contradict in some measure the following adjective ἄκρατος ‘full strength, pure’ (LN 79.99).

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: the hard bony outgrowth on the heads of certain animals
s.c: Finding a term for ‘horn’ is usually not at all difficult. The problem arises when a term for ‘horn’ is already employed in a receptor language as a euphemistic expression for the male genital organ. It may therefore be necessary in ⟦Revelation 5:6|Revelation 5:6⟧ to speak of ‘a lamb with seven horns on his head.’|In speaking of the horn-shaped corners of the altar (⟦Revelation 9:13|Revelation 9:13⟧), it is often better not to use a term meaning literally horn, since this might imply that the altar had the horns of animals stuck on to the corners. One can normally say ‘corners of the altar shaped like horns’ or ‘… looking like horns or projections on the corners of the altar.’ See LN 79.105.

s.d: a projection at the corner of an object
(a figurative extension of meaning of {L:κέρας<SDBG:κέρας:000000>}[a] ‘horn,’ {D:8.17}) power of unusual significance
s.c: In ⟦Luke 1:69|Luke 1:69⟧ the reference of the phrase κέρας σωτηρίας is to the role of the Messiah, and accordingly one may often best render this phrase as ‘mighty Savior’ or ‘powerful Savior.’

s.d: (a diminutive derivative of {L:κέρας<SDBG:κέρας:000000>}[a] ‘horn,’ {D:8.17}) the pod of the carob tree (which closely resembles a small horn)
s.c: Carob pods were commonly used for fattening swine and were employed as an article of food by poor people. In translating ⟦Luke 15:16|Luke 15:16⟧ it is not necessary, however, to identify specifically carob pods. In most languages some such expression as ‘edible pods’ is probably more satisfactory, since carob trees are unlikely to be known.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Earn, Gain, Do Business
s.d: to gain by means of one’s activity or investment
s.g: to earn; to gain; to make a profit

s.d: to cause a loss not to happen{N:001}
s.g: to avoid; to cause not to occur

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Earn, Gain, Do Business
s.d: (derivative of {L:κερδαίνω<SDBG:κερδαίνω:000000>}[a] ‘to earn, to gain,’ {D:57.189}) that which is gained or earned
s.c: κέρδος in the sense of ‘gain’ is not restricted, however, to monetary gain or profit. It may refer to any kind of benefit or advantage, for example, ἐμοὶ γὰρ τὸ ζῆν Χριστὸς καὶ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν κέρδος ‘for me life is Christ, and death is a gain’ ⟦Philippians 1:21|Philippians 1:21⟧.

s.d: coins of lesser value

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Earn, Gain, Do Business
s.d: one who exchanges currency, either in terms of different types of currency or different values of the same currency
a brief statement of the main point of a previously given discourse

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Pay, Price, Cost
s.d: a sum of money

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: uppermost part of the human body, or the front or upper part of the body of an animal, typically separated from the rest of the body by a neck, and containing the brain, mouth, and sense organs; associated with the entire person, that person’s life and responsibilities
s.c: In some languages it may be necessary to distinguish clearly between the head which is still a part of a body and a severed head. It is this latter meaning which is obviously involved in ⟦Mark 6:25|Mark 6:25⟧.|In rendering ⟦1 Corinthians 11:4|1 Corinthians 11:4⟧, πᾶς ἀνὴρ προσευχόμενος ἢ προφητεύων κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων ‘any man who prays or prophesies with his head covered,’ it may be important to indicate that the covering is not one which is designed to cover the entire head including the face, but only the top of the head. The same applies, of course, to ⟦1 Corinthians 11:5|1 Corinthians 11:5⟧ and ⟦1 Corinthians 11:7|1 Corinthians 11:7⟧.

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:κεφαλή<SDBG:κεφαλή:000000>}[a] ‘head,’ {D:8.10}) one who is of supreme or pre-eminent status, in view of authority to order or command
s.g: one who is the head of; one who is superior to; one who is supreme over

s.dp: Constructions › Parts and Areas of Buildings
s.d: (a set phrase, literally: head of the corner) the cornerstone or capstone of a building, essential to its construction (κεφαλὴ γωνίας occurs in the NT only figuratively in reference to Christ)
s.c: Though some scholars have thought that κεφαλὴ γωνίας refers to a keystone of an arch or the lintel stone over a door, it is highly probable that κεφαλὴ γωνίας has essentially the same meaning as ἀκρογωνιαῖος.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Tire, Rest
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to lay down the head) to experience the rest which comes from sleep
s.g: to lie down to rest; to lie down to sleep
s.c: ὁ δὲ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἔχει ποῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν κλίνω ‘the Son of Man has no place to lie down to rest’ ⟦Matthew 8:20|Matthew 8:20⟧, implies that Jesus possessed no permanent home. In ⟦John 19:30|John 19:30⟧ this same expression must be understood not as an idiom but as a case of literally bowing the head (see LN 16.16).

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to have down on the head) to wear a covering over one’s head
s.g: to have one’s head covered; to cover one’s head

s.d: to beat someone on the head, implying repeated blows

s.dp: Artifacts › Instruments Used in Marking and Writing
s.d: section of a scroll or of a long composition
s.c: Long compositions often involved several scrolls, and a κεφαλίς would form one section or scroll of such a composition.|In the case of practically all terms for documents (for example, ‘letter,’ ‘book,’ ‘scroll’) the meaning involves not only the object on which the writing was done, but also the contents of the writing. In some languages a distinction must be made between these two aspects of such objects, and one must make certain that the particular expression used in a receptor language will at least include the contents and not refer merely to the materials on which the words may have been written.

s.d: (a borrowing from Latin) a tax paid by each adult male to the government
s.c: See discussion at LN 57.179.

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Pastures and Cultivated Lands
s.d: a field used for the cultivation of herbs, fruits, flowers, or vegetables
one who takes care of a garden or orchard
(derivative of {L:κηρύσσω<SDBG:κηρύσσω:000002>}[c] ‘to preach,’ {D:33.256}) the content of what is preached
(derivative of {L:κηρύσσω<SDBG:κηρύσσω:000002>}[c] ‘to preach,’ {D:33.256}) a person who preaches
to announce in a formal or official manner by means of a herald or one who functions as a herald
to announce extensively and publicly
to publicly announce religious truths and principles while urging acceptance and compliance{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages it is impossible to translate κηρύσσω without indicating the content of what is preached. Accordingly, one may have such expressions as to preach about the good news or to preach about God.

s.dp: Animals › Fishes and Other Sea Creatures
s.d: any large sea creature

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the Aramaic equivalent of the Greek name {L:Πέτρος<SDBG:Πέτρος:000000>} ‘Peter’ ({D:93.296})

s.dp: Artifacts › Boats and Parts of Boats
s.d: a large box-like structure (the vessel built by Noah)
s.c: The central meaning of κιβωτός is ‘box’ or ‘chest,’ but it was apparently applied to Noah’s ark in view of the type of construction and the fact that Noah’s ark resembled more a barge than a seagoing vessel. However, in view of the size of Noah’s ark, it is probably best in most languages to speak of it as a ‘ship.’

s.d: any box-like container, whether plain or elaborate; here, refers to the box used to hold the tablets of the Law
s.c: In the NT κιβωτός occurs only in the phrase κιβωτὸς τῆς διαθήκης ‘the box of the covenant,’ which was placed in the Holy of Holies of the Temple in Jerusalem and referred to also as being in the heavenly temple (⟦Revelation 11:19|Revelation 11:19⟧).|In the case of English some persons object to speaking of the so-called ‘ark of the Covenant’ as ‘the Covenant Box,’ since they assume that the English word ‘ark’ has some special meaning equivalent to the corresponding Greek or Hebrew terms. However, the term ‘ark’ in Old English and Middle English is simply a borrowing of Latin arca meaning ‘box, chest, coffer.’ In present-day English the term ark is known primarily from the context of ‘Noah’s ark.’

s.d: a small stringed harp-like instrument held in the hands and plucked
s.c: The closest equivalent to a κιθάρα is in most instances a small harp.

s.d: (derivative of {L:κιθάρα<SDBG:κιθάρα:000000>} lyre, harp, {D:6.83}) to play a lyre, a small stringed harp-like instrument held in the hands and plucked
s.g: to play a lyre; to play a harp

s.d: (derivative of {L:κιθαρίζω<SDBG:κιθαρίζω:000000>} ‘to play a lyre,’ {D:6.84}) one who plays the lyre, a small stringed harp-like instrument held in the hands and plucked

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a province in the southeast corner of Asia Minor
to be in dangerous circumstances

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Expose Oneself to Danger
s.d: to expose oneself to danger
a state of dangerous and threatening circumstances
to make a change of location in space (a highly generic meaning)
s.g: to move; to come; to go
s.c: A strictly literal translation of κινέω in ⟦Acts 17:28|Acts 17:28⟧ might imply merely moving from one place to another. The meaning, however, is generalized movement and activity; therefore, it may be possible to translate κινούμεθα as ‘we come and go’ or ‘we move about’ or even ‘we do what we do.’

s.d: to cause something to be moved from a place
s.c: It is also possible to translate κινέω in ⟦Revelation 2:5|Revelation 2:5⟧ as ‘I will take away.’

s.d: to set something in motion, with the nature of the movement dependent upon the object in question
s.c: In ⟦Mark 15:29|Mark 15:29⟧ the shaking of the head signifies derision and scorn, but in some languages this meaning is expressed by quite different gestures, for example, pointing with the finger, throwing back the head, or shrugging the shoulders. In fact, in some languages shaking the head from side to side means assent, while nodding shows opposition.

s.d: to cause people to riot against
s.g: to stir up against; to start a riot; to cause an uproar

s.dp: Case › Agent in a Causative Role Marked by Verbs
s.d: a marker of a causative relation, with the implication of significant activity
a type of spice derived from the bark of certain aromatic plants
s.c: In most languages κιννάμωμον is simply borrowed in a transliterated form. However, it is also possible to use a type of descriptive phrase, for example, ‘good-tasting bark’ or ‘flavoring bark.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the father of King Saul
a secondary woody stem arising from the trunk or bough of a tree or shrub
s.g: branch (of a tree or woody shrub)
s.c: Some languages distinguish carefully between two major types of branches those which are essentially leaves (as in the case of palms) and those which have a number of buds or potential branches. Other languages may make a distinction between branches of a plant which is woody (a perennial) and those which are relatively soft and flexible, typical of an annual plant.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Laugh, Cry, Groan
s.d: to weep or wail, with emphasis upon the noise accompanying the weeping
s.g: to weep; to wail; to lament; weeping; crying
s.c: In ⟦Matthew 2:18|Matthew 2:18⟧ κλαίω occurs with a so-called ‘direct object,’ for example, Ραχὴλ κλαίουσα τὰ τέκνα αὐτῆς … ὅτι οὐκ εἰσίν ‘Rachel weeps for her children … because they are all dead.’ The so-called direct object is, however, the cause of the weeping, and the so-called transitive usage of κλαίω does not alter the meaning.
